question.text:
Given below are two statements labeled as Assertion and Reason. Choose the correct option from the given choices.

Assertion: A particle moving with constant acceleration cannot have its average velocity equal to zero over any duration.
Reason: For the average velocity of a moving object to vanish, its non-zero velocity must not stay unchanging.

options.1: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
options.2: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
options.3: Assertion is true, but Reason is false.
options.4: Assertion is false, but Reason is true.

solution.approach: Test the claim with a ball thrown up and caught at the same point; the average velocity over the trip is zero even though the acceleration is uniform throughout.

steps.text: Take a ball thrown upward at 20 m/s under gravity g = 10 m/s², a constant, uniform acceleration throughout its flight.
Find the total time of flight, up and back down to the same starting height.
Find the net displacement over this time; it returns exactly to the starting point.
The average velocity is this net displacement divided by the time, giving zero even though the acceleration was uniform and nonzero throughout, so the Assertion is false.

The Reason correctly states that average velocity can only be zero when the velocity does not stay a fixed nonzero value throughout, which is a true condition, so the Reason is true even though the Assertion is false.

final_answer.value: If Assertion is false but the Reason is true.

common_mistakes.text: Assuming uniform acceleration always produces a changing, nonzero average velocity, missing the case of a body that returns to its starting point.
